body.statement:
Under the primitive sequential-randomization, availability, positivity, boundedness, and control-total-variation conditions, the universally valid comparison is
\[
 \eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)
 \le \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \le 2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
No constant \(c_\alpha>0\) depending only on \(\alpha\) can strengthen the left side to \(c_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\) uniformly over this primitive adaptive-design class, even when \(B=3\), \(W=\{2\}\), and \(\Gamma=0\).  A matching radius comparison is recovered on the following structurally restricted but explicitly checkable adaptive subclass.  Let \(Y^{(0)}\) be the all-zero schedule.  Suppose there is a set \(S\subseteq\{(b,i)\in\mathcal T:b\in W\}\) with
\[
 w(S):=\sum_{(b,i)\in S}\frac{q_b}{n_b},
 \qquad
 2M w(S)\ge\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star,
 \qquad
 P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^{(0)}}
 \{Z_{bi}\ne z_1\text{ for every }(b,i)\in S\}
 \ge1-\eta_\alpha.
\]
Then
\[
 \eta_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star
 \le \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \le 2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
The reachability probability is the finite-tree sum of the known sequential path probabilities on zero-outcome histories avoiding \(z_1\) at the positions in \(S\); the design may remain history adaptive away from that subtree.  The choice \(S=\{(b,i):b\in W\}\) has \(w(S)=1\) and therefore gives the simpler sufficient condition that the focal arm is avoided throughout its window with probability at least \(1-\eta_\alpha\).  Coverage and expected length in all displays use the same extended law, and the infimum ranges over every schedule-independent auxiliary-randomized, variable-length observed-data interval kernel.
body.justification: The theorem now gives the strongest valid operational statement: a generic factor-two constructive upper bound and mixture-modulus lower bound, an explicit impossibility certificate for unrestricted radius equivalence, and a derived matching sandwich on a finite-tree adaptive reachability subclass.
body.gap: Gaussian and model-based platform results do not capture the rare-history expected-length obstruction.  The unrestricted comparison is false, while the new masked-history certificate supplies a positive theorem without assuming the crux.
body.consumer: The NCC implementation can always report the projected uniformly honest interval.  It should advertise minimax equivalence to the optimized radius only after computing and passing the masked-history reachability check; otherwise it should report the generic modulus lower bound and flag rare adaptive branches as a limitation.
body.proof_tex:
The upper inequality is exactly the operational consequence of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:honest\text{-}upper\text{-}frontier}\).  That theorem constructs one schedule-independent kernel \(K^\star\in\mathcal C_\alpha\) and proves
\[
 \sup_{Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,\Gamma}}
 \mathbb E^{K^\star}_{\mathcal D,Y}
 [\operatorname{len}(I^\star)]
 \le2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(K\in\mathcal C_\alpha\), exactly as prescribed by Definition \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}minimax\text{-}length}\), gives
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\le2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]

For the unconditional lower inequality, \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) implies
\[
 \eta_\alpha=\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}
 \in(0,1-2\alpha).
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:mixture\text{-}modulus\text{-}length\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\), applied at this value, therefore gives
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \ge\eta_\alpha
 \Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha).
\]
Both inequalities hold for every design and fixed-schedule class satisfying the primitive assumptions.

Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:rare\text{-}history\text{-}alpha\text{-}only\text{-}obstruction}\) constructs admissible designs for which
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\longrightarrow0.
\]
If a positive \(c_\alpha\), depending only on \(\alpha\), satisfied \(c_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\) uniformly over the primitive class, division by the positive quantity \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\) would give \(c_\alpha\le\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\) for every \(n\), contradicting the displayed limit.  This proves the generic obstruction.

Now impose the stated masked-history reachability condition.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:masked\text{-}focal\text{-}modulus\text{-}certificate}\), with \(\gamma=\Gamma\), gives
\[
 \Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\ge2M w(S).
\]
Combining this with the already proved mixture-modulus lower bound yields
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge2\eta_\alpha M w(S).
\]
The structural weight condition \(2M w(S)\ge\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\), together with \(\eta_\alpha>0\), therefore implies
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \ge2\eta_\alpha M w(S)
 \ge\eta_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
Together with the universal factor-two upper bound, this is the claimed restricted-class equivalence.  The masked-modulus lemma derives its testing pair from the finite adaptive tree; no radius-to-modulus comparison is assumed.
